threat: Attacker reads or changes source code stored in S3
vulnerability: WAF/CDN poorly configured, so the bucket can be reached directly or is over-permissive
planned_actions: Least-privilege IAM, TLS, firewall hardening, CI/CD guardrails

threat: Attacker takes over an employee account and tampers with database data
vulnerability: Login uses password + OTP only (no enforced MFA); malware can steal session cookies
planned_actions: MFA and passkeys, endpoint protection, short session lifetimes

threat: DDoS makes the production app unavailable
vulnerability: No rate limiting or DDoS protection in front of the app
planned_actions: Rate limiting plus a DDoS protection service/CDN

threat: Attacker exploits known weaknesses in the app or its components
vulnerability: Unpatched vulnerabilities; no regular patch schedule

threat: Malicious code reaches production through the pipeline or a third-party dependency
vulnerability: Broad deploy permissions and no mandatory review, so a compromised account or library can push code
planned_actions: Mandatory approval step, automated scanners, third-party audits

threat: Man-in-the-middle attacker reads or alters traffic between staff on public Wi-Fi and the app
vulnerability: TLS not enforced everywhere; weak TLS versions and no HSTS

threat: Credential stuffing: attacker logs in with passwords leaked from other breaches
vulnerability: Password + OTP login only; no login rate limiting or breached-password checks
planned_actions: Passkeys/MFA, login rate limiting, breached-password checks

threat: Attacker steals customer personal data from the database
vulnerability: Broad database access and no encryption at rest
planned_actions: Encryption at rest, least-privilege access, access logging

threat: Ransomware or an attacker deletes or encrypts backups
vulnerability: Backups share an account with production; restores never tested
planned_actions: Separate-account immutable backups, quarterly restore tests

vulnerability: Limited central logging; no alerting or monitoring
planned_actions: Central logging, threat detection, alerts to an on-call channel

threat: Phishing tricks an employee into giving up credentials or running malware
vulnerability: No security awareness training or phishing simulations
planned_actions: Onboarding training, quarterly phishing simulations, passkeys

threat: Vendor breach exposes Skylance customer data
vulnerability: No vendor risk assessment or data processing agreements
planned_actions: Contracts and DPAs shifting liability; vendor questionnaire and annual review of key vendors

threat: Slow, chaotic response to a security incident
vulnerability: No documented incident response plan or roles
planned_actions: Incident response policy, defined roles, yearly tabletop exercise

threat: Customer data exposed through the less-protected QA/test environments
vulnerability: Real production data is copied into QA/test with weaker controls
planned_actions: CI/CD pipeline rebuild with RBAC enforced, WORM storage/sandboxing for QA/test, masked or synthetic data
